notes: Coupling efficiency depends on matching precatalyst, base, and solvent with the electrophile and boron partner.
Refer to individual playbooks for ligand selection and stability guidance.

playbooks.name: Pd(PPh3)4 benchmark
notes: Maintain an equimolar Pd to phosphine ratio to favor mono-ligated Pd(0) that accelerates transmetallation.
scope_limitations: Electron-poor chlorides and strongly coordinating heterocycles need more donating ligands or stronger bases.

evidence.quote: Thus, fastest transmetallation was observed with one equivalent of a more electron deficient mono-phosphine ligand consistent with transmetallation being the rate determining step.
A combination of Pd(PPh3)4 or PdCl2(PPh3)2 and aqueous Na2CO3 in dimethoxyethane works satisfactorily in most cases.

playbooks.name: Pd2(dba)3 + SPhos
notes: Maintain an equimolar Pd to phosphine ratio to favor mono-ligated Pd(0) that accelerates transmetallation.
scope_limitations: Electron-poor chlorides and strongly coordinating heterocycles need more donating ligands or stronger bases.

evidence.quote: Thus, fastest transmetallation was observed with one equivalent of a more electron deficient mono-phosphine ligand consistent with transmetallation being the rate determining step.

playbooks.name: Pd2(dba)3 + XPhos for ortho aryl bromides
notes: Bulky biaryl ligands enforce mono-ligation and create a pocket that accommodates ortho substituents.
scope_limitations: Extreme steric clash or acid-sensitive substituents may require lower base strength or alternative ligands.

evidence.quote: The Buchwald group developed an exceptional Pd catalyst for the Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of challenging aryl halides. An electron-rich biaryl ligand 95 was designed to provide the necessary steric interactions and electron density.

playbooks.name: Ligand 95 high steric protocol
notes: Bulky biaryl ligands enforce mono-ligation and create a pocket that accommodates ortho substituents.
scope_limitations: Extreme steric clash or acid-sensitive substituents may require lower base strength or alternative ligands.

evidence.quote: Employing this ligand, cross-coupling between sterically hindered aryl halides and aryl boronic acids or alkylboranes was accomplished with low catalyst loadings.

playbooks.name: XPhos for electron-poor aryl chlorides
notes: Use strongly donating, bulky ligands to accelerate oxidative addition into C-Cl and ensure adequate base strength for boronate activation.
scope_limitations: Coordinating heterocycles can slow oxidative addition; additives such as fluoride may be required when protodeboronation competes.

evidence.quote: Chlorobenzene derivatives are generally quite inert to oxidative addition, but some pi-difficient heteroaryl chlorides give coupling products.

playbooks.name: Ligand 95 for electron-rich aryl chlorides
notes: Electron-rich biaryl ligands balance steric bulk and donor capacity to push oxidative addition of unactivated C-Cl bonds.
scope_limitations: When base-sensitive groups are present, swap to milder phosphate or carbonate salts and consider lower temperature.

evidence.quote: Employing this ligand, cross-coupling between sterically hindered aryl halides and aryl boronic acids or alkylboranes was accomplished with low catalyst loadings.

playbooks.name: PdCl2(dppf) triflate coupling
notes: Powdered K3PO4 in aprotic solvent efficiently promotes triflate couplings; boronic acids outperform esters for arylations.
scope_limitations: Moisture accelerates hydrolysis of activated triflates; exclude water unless using slow-release boron sources.

evidence.quote: Powdered K3PO4 suspended in THF or dioxane is sufficient to accelerate the coupling of 9-alkyl-9-BBN, 1-alkenyl-, and arylboronates or boronic acids with triflates.

playbooks.name: 2-pyridyl slow-release strategy
notes: Combine rapid-activation precatalysts, copper additives, masking ligands, and slow-release hydrolysis to keep free boronic acid levels low.
scope_limitations: Excess water accelerates MIDA hydrolysis beyond control; maintain biphasic solvent ratios and add base gradually.

evidence.quote: A precatalyst was employed that undergoes rapid activation to directly form a highly active mono-coordinated XPhos-ligated palladium(0) complex.
The 2-pyridyl MIDA boronate steadily hydrolyses throughout the coupling, reducing exposure of the liberated boronic acid to protodeboronation.

playbooks.name: Pd(PPh3)4 with diethyl(3-pyridyl)borane
notes: Air-stable diethyl boranes simplify handling; phase-transfer salts keep the boronate engaged in biphasic media.
scope_limitations: Hydrolytic deboronation increases under fully aqueous conditions; retain an organic co-solvent.

evidence.quote: Diethyl(3-pyridyl)borane synthesized by Terashima is a unique air-stable reagent for heteroarylation.

playbooks.name: Lithium triisopropylboronate strategy

when.substrate_class: Thiophene and furan derivatives susceptible to protodeboronation

notes: Preformed lithium triisopropylboronates resist protodeboronation and remain active after extended storage.
scope_limitations: Limited solubility in nonpolar solvents; include minor water fractions or polar co-solvents for activation.

evidence.quote: Lithium triisopropylboronates are stabilized by Lewis-base coordination and are more resistant to protodeboronation than regular boronic acids, especially for 2-heteroaryl substrates.

playbooks.name: dan borane activation with KOtBu
notes: Strong, bulky alkoxide bases generate the active boronate required for transmetallation; potassium cations stabilize the transition state.
scope_limitations: Sodium or lithium tert-butoxide fail to form the reactive boronate; maintain strict exclusion of moisture.

evidence.quote: Only potassium tert-butanolate and not the corresponding sodium or lithium base promoted formation of the boronate required for transmetallation.

playbooks.name: PdCl2(dppf) for vinyl halides
notes: Run at room temperature with acetate base to suppress cis/trans isomerization during coupling.
scope_limitations: More basic media trigger beta-elimination; avoid strong bases with sensitive vinyl halides.

evidence.quote: PdCl2(dppf) is effective for carrying out the reaction at room temperature in order to depress isomerization during the coupling.

playbooks.name: Benzylic/allylic couplings with disiamylborane
notes: Hydroboration followed by Suzuki coupling furnishes 1,4-dienes and allylbenzenes with controlled branched-to-linear ratios.
scope_limitations: Pd(PPh3)4 can deactivate in very polar media; keep a biphasic organic layer to maintain catalyst activity.

evidence.quote: Hydroboration of alkynes with disiamylborane, followed by cross-coupling with allylic or benzylic halides in the presence of Pd(PPh3)4 and aqueous NaOH produces 1,4-alkadienes or allylbenzenes in high yields.

playbooks.name: Primary alkyl iodides with 9-BBN
notes: Triphenylphosphine-bound palladium minimizes beta-hydride elimination when run at 60 °C with excess phosphate base.
scope_limitations: Bidentate phosphines slow reductive elimination; avoid dppe, dppp, or dppb for these substrates.

evidence.quote: The palladium complex with triphenylphosphine as ligand is recognized to be most effective for cross-coupling between 9-alkyl-9-BBN and primary iodoalkanes.

playbooks.name: Chiral secondary alkyl Bpin with Ag2O
notes: Silver(I) additives scavenge halide and promote transmetallation, allowing retention of stereochemistry at room temperature.
scope_limitations: Coordinating functional groups on the alkyl fragment can trigger inversion; maintain inert atmosphere and exclude protic impurities.

evidence.quote: Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of chiral secondary alkylboronic esters with aryl iodides in the presence of Pd2(dba)3 and Ag2O afforded products in high yields with retention of configuration.

playbooks.name: Miyaura borylation of aryl halides
notes: Pd-catalysed borylation furnishes boronic esters in one step, providing modular access to downstream Suzuki couplings.
scope_limitations: Hydride-sensitive functional groups may undergo reduction; consider lower temperatures or alternative bases.

evidence.quote: The palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling of (alkoxy)diboron derivatives provides a one-step procedure for arylboronic esters from aryl halides.

playbooks.name: Micellar Ni nanoparticle coupling

when.substrate_class: Aryl halides with micellar Ni catalysis

notes: Designer surfactant TPGS-750-M retains the catalyst in water, enabling low organic solvent usage and facile product extraction.
scope_limitations: Hydrophobic substrates may require small co-solvent charges; maintain surfactant concentration to avoid deactivation.

evidence.quote: They used a designer surfactant TPGS-750-M engineered to remain in the water phase during in-flask extraction, requiring minimal organic solvent.

priors.comment: Protodeboronation risk increases away from the stability plateau; monitor pH and consider masking strategies.
